A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distractor-generation framework and CLOTH study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset augmentation, model evaluations, ablations, and studies with ESL learners and proficient English users, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports ESL answer-selection frequencies and automatic–human evaluation agreement.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the described attention calculation from using the last generated token as the query to accumulating attention across all generated answer tokens. This revises one component of information restriction; the generation, filtering, clustering, and multitask framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English word-level cloze distractors using original and augmented CLOTH data, including CLOTH-M/H examples and the five-ESL-learner and ten-expert studies. New demographics and answer-selection results describe retained coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain GPT-4o in zero- and five-shot settings, CDGP and Text2Text, the same deletion-strategy alternatives, and the same normalization comparators. Text2Text already appears in v1 Table 9 despite receiving clearer discussion in v2.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the stated calibration sample source from augmented test data to validation data, although v2 subsequently still calls it a 'labeled test set.' Section 3.2 changes sampled distractors to entire difficulty subsets for training. v2 also adds a Spearman agreement evaluation on the existing 50 human-evaluation questions. These statements do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds an analysis of agreement between GPT-4o and human difficulty rankings, alongside ESL answer-selection analysis. The deletion-ratio and deletion-strategy studies, multitask ablations, normalization comparison, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first quantifies annotation agreement, reporting GPT–human correlation of 0.54 and inter-human agreement of 0.62. Existing mean and standard-deviation reporting remains; no new seed, repeated-run, or confidence-interval reporting is provided.

E6.justification: New results include ESL selection frequencies in v2 Table 8, including 8.6% for hard distractors versus 1.6% for original distractors, agreement statistics, and 2% grammatical-filter rejection. Prose corrections include augmented hard-distractor invalidity from 3.0% to 4.2% and multitask Hardest frequency from 73.65% to 73.25%, matching retained tables. Table 3 expresses the same proportions on a 0–1 scale.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1, its deletion-count rule, and the existing normalization reasoning are retained. Appendix B adds explanatory variable references without introducing new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: two-way augmentation, difficulty-aware multitask generation, improved difficulty control relative to GPT-4o, and release of the dataset and model.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets difficulty as contextual semantic plausibility and uses the new analyses to support ESL applicability and GPT-4o evaluator reliability. Section 7 softens earlier warnings about continuous difficulty and fixed-threshold inconsistencies, emphasizing expert-calibrated binary difficulty instead.

D1.justification: v2 adds the GPT-4o generation prompt and five-shot construction details, QA batch size 8, early-stopping disclosures, STS filtering implementation, calibration-expert qualifications, and annotator demographics and compensation information. The resource link changes from an anonymous repository to GitHub. These additions mostly document existing procedures.

R1.justification: Section 2 strengthens positioning against IRT approaches by emphasizing unverified human/model parameter correspondence in cloze tasks and computational demands. It also shortens discussion of Wang et al.'s augmentation and multitask contributions. The bibliography retains the same cited works.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites across the abstract, methods, results, and limitations, plus updated affiliations and acknowledgments. New prompt and annotation appendices accompany relocation of the invalid-ratio discussion into the main text; the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds ESL answer-selection and demographic tables and a GPT-4o generation-prompt figure. The invalid-ratio table moves from v1 Appendix H to the main text. Figure 4 changes colors and legend order while retaining its curves; other displays undergo limited relocation and caption editing.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through additional prompts, training details, and annotator documentation, adds an evaluator-agreement check, and corrects several numerical statements. The gain is limited: most results are unchanged, the F1 prose/table discrepancy and ambiguous calibration wording remain, and the revised limitations soften earlier warnings about binary difficulty.
